log.hypothesis: Baseline activations of the original model on 256 soft1e-3 jets, to get per-channel residual statistics, readouts of pid/log_pt/log_E and the added photon token's representation.
Residual streams entering each body block and classifier block, to compute queries and pick a saturated key pattern that every query scores very negatively.
Residual streams entering each body block and classifier block, to compute queries and pick a saturated key pattern that every query scores very negatively.

Exact detector (embed step units -> 3 scratch channels -> block0 AND units) drives flagged tokens to a saturated corner whose keys score ~-2..-12 for all queries; should remove most of the soft-neutral effect, leaving the kNN and block0-attention leaks.
Original model on reco(soft1e-3): the target activations for the v1 comparison.
v1 on raw soft1e-3; the gap to 005 at block0 measures the kNN + block0-attention leak, later sites the incomplete key suppression.

Same detector as v1, but the flagged token's saturated pattern is tuned for block 1 and rewritten by a dead block-1 unit to a pattern tuned for blocks 2-7 and the classifier; stronger key suppression should lower E_rule.
Find MLP hidden units in blocks 1-7 whose pre-activation stays below about -6 on every real token; those output exactly 0 and can be repurposed as per-block rewrite units at no cost.
Find MLP hidden units in blocks 1-7 whose pre-activation stays below about -6 on every real token; those output exactly 0 and can be repurposed as per-block rewrite units at no cost.
v2 on raw soft1e-3 vs original on reco (005): locate the residual gap (block0 leak vs later blocks).

v2 plus a veto that blocks flagging when log E < log pT (impossible in real data, frequent in noised jets) via a 4th scratch channel; E_rule should stay ~0.13 while gen_drift falls by roughly a third.
Original block-0 MLP inputs on jets with one added photon/neutral hadron spanning the thresholds; used to refit the pid readouts and channel folds on a broader token population.
Check of the v2 detector on the same tokens: photon/NH flag units should be positive exactly on rule-dropped tokens, restore units exact.
v2 with pid readouts and folds refit on 1280 jets incl. soft neutral hadrons and wider gate margins; E_rule ~ v2, side effects ~ v2.

v4 without folding the scratch channels out of the existing block-0 MLP units: smaller DoF; kept soft particles see a saturated scratch read, so clean e_v and side effects rise somewhat; E_rule ~unchanged.
v4 with saturated patterns chosen from 8x16 head geometry with summary/particle queries normalised separately; slightly different trade-off, E_rule within +-0.02 of v4.
v4 with the scratch reads of existing block-0 units replaced by their mean (bias fold) instead of a linear fold: DoF between v4s and v4, E_rule between 0.13 and 0.22.
v5 pattern but particle-query heads weighted 3x more than summary-query heads.
v5 pattern but summary-query heads weighted 10x (classifier reads summary tokens).
v5 without the linear fold (small DoF variant); E_rule rises as for v4s.

Control: v5 detector, scratch channels, folds and restores, but flag write L=0 (no suppression). Isolates generator drift caused by the scratch machinery on noised tokens from drift caused by flagging.
Sensor test: only the three block-0 restore units (fire iff a scratch read exceeds 0.65, never at t=0). Nonzero gen_drift means they misfire on the time token or noised tokens at t>0.
Sensor test: only the linear fold of the scratch channels into the other block-0 inputs. Drift here measures out-of-distribution fold error on noised/time tokens.

v5 with scratch moved off channel 116 (where the time token is massive) to 17/122/87 and the fold fit without time-massive predictor channels; generator drift from the fold should drop from ~0.08 while E_rule stays ~0.10.
Small variant: no fold, scratch on the three cheapest channels (122, 87, 4: summed read weight 21 vs 49), so kept soft particles are perturbed about half as much as in v5s.

Same circuit as v7s (no fold, scratch 122/87/4, v5 patterns) but written with minimal entries: dead units keep their old rows/norm weights, single-entry fc1/fc2 writes scaled by the old norm weight, a 64-channel pid readout, and a 40-channel block-1 rewrite detector. E_rule and side effects ~v7s, DoF ~480.
Check v8's detector on P jets (flag units positive exactly on rule-dropped tokens) and record activations to compare with the original on reco(P).
Original model on reco(P): target activations for the P-probe gap analysis.
v8 circuit with the particle-weighted saturated patterns (as v6a): lower E_rule at the same size, higher generator drift.

v8 with the blocks-2-7 pattern also chosen so the flagged token's fixed body output scores very negatively as a key in generator block 0 (mean logit -0.8 -> -3.0). If generator drift comes from generator attention to flagged tokens, drift falls; E_rule ~0.10.
Mix: particle-weighted block-1 pattern (v9) with the v8 blocks-2-7 pattern; tells whether v9's gain and drift come from block 1.
Mix: v8 block-1 pattern with the particle-weighted blocks-2-7 pattern.
Blocks-2-7 pattern: particle queries weight 1, body summary 0.3, classifier summary 1. Expect between v8 and v12.
Blocks-2-7 pattern: stronger particle emphasis (summary 0.1, classifier 0.3). Expect E_rule <= v12, drift high.

v8 plus a plausibility step (log E >= log pT - 0.008, true for every real particle) as an extra AND input of both flags, on scratch channel 4; E22 step moved to channel 116. No flag on implausible noised tokens -> generator drift down ~30%; channel 4 now reads +1 for every particle in block-0 MLP (cheap channel, S=2.4) so clean side effects rise slightly.
v15 with channel 4 linearly folded out of the existing block-0 units (R2 0.997) to remove the side effect of the always-on plausibility write.

v8 plus linear fold of its scratch channels (122,87,4; time-light channels) out of the existing block-0 units: removes the kept-soft-token perturbation; E_rule ~0.095, drift close to v8 since these channels carry little time-token signal.
Original logits on new probes (soft NH; 3 soft photons) + 512 clean jets (for S).
